question: Who said, "Literacy in itself is not Education"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Mahatma Gandhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** emphasized that literacy alone is not sufficient for education.
 
• He believed that true education involves the holistic development of a person, including moral and ethical values.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of education, known as **Nai Talim** or Basic Education, integrated intellectual, physical, and spiritual aspects of learning.
 
• He argued that education should be rooted in the culture and environment of the learner, promoting self-reliance and practical skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the **Father of the Nation**, played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence.
 
• His principles of **non-violence (Ahimsa)** and **truth (Satya)** guided his approach to both political and social issues.
 
• Gandhi's influence extended beyond India, inspiring global movements for civil rights and freedom.
 
• His legacy continues to impact contemporary discussions on education, social justice, and ethical leadership.
